clue.text: Cable a curate, distraught about a test result

indicators.note: about tells us the shuffled letters are wrapped round the second a in the clue
distraught means upset and in disarray, so the letters of cable a curate are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman and his cable are oddly linked to the anxious wait for an exam result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container: the jumbled letters wrap the second 'a'. 'test result' is fair because the baccalaureate is the qualification an exam awards.
explanation.definitionFit: The baccalaureate is an examination qualification, so passing it is the outcome of a test.

clue.text: Car gets very good parking space for George

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
a car lot is a parking area

explanation.surface: A motorist acquires an excellent spot to leave the car for a man called George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is old RAF and pilots' slang for the automatic pilot, so the name is the definition, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen nicknamed the automatic flight-control system 'George', who flies the plane while the crew rest.

clue.text: Healed by crude manipulation

indicators.note: manipulation means handling and reshaping, so the letters of crude are worked into another order

explanation.surface: Someone was made well by rough handling from a bonesetter.
explanation.definitionFit: To heal someone and to make them better after illness are the same act, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Sailing off, one included in networking

indicators.note: included in tells us the numeral letter goes inside the rearranged sailing
off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of sailing are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A yacht leaves harbour with one more guest added to the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SAILING; 'included in' then slips I (one) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Liaising is making contact and working with others, which is what networking involves.

clue.text: Bill in outstanding condition?

parts.note: outstanding seems to praise a bill in excellent shape, but it means still owed, so the clue describes an invoice nobody has settled

explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like 'excellent', but for a bill it means 'not yet paid'.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice that remains outstanding has not been settled by the debtor.

clue.text: Onset of epilepsy may precipitate hepatitis? Yes, sadly mother has health problem

indicators.note: onset is the beginning, so we take the first letter of each of the next four words
sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, so the letters of yes are jumbled

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A gloomy medical chain: epilepsy may bring on hepatitis, and poor mother falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onset of' covers four words: epilepsy, may, precipitate, hepatitis, giving EMPH; 'sadly' turns YES into YSE; then MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphysema is a chronic lung disease that causes breathlessness, an illness.

clue.text: Row about black flower

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a row wraps round the colour's letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a dark-coloured bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword code for a river (a thing that flows); the Tiber runs through Rome. 'Row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, which is the crossword sense of flower; the Tiber is Rome's river.

clue.text: In these old photographs ray's group teed off

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of place, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Snaps from long ago show a band led by Ray setting off on a golf round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges RAYS GROUP TEED; the grid's spelling drops the second E of the usual form, a recognised variant.
explanation.definitionFit: These were early images fixed on silvered copper plates, the first popular form of photography in the 1840s.

clue.text: Erin's overcoat abandoned in college

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters of Erin's overcoat run free into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl's coat has been left behind at her school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' suggests left behind, but here means wild, rearranging ERINS OVERCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatoire is a specialist school of music, a type of college.

clue.text: Following death, a politician reveals old mining hazard

parts.note: after means following in time
D is the abbreviation for died or death, as in genealogies
MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: After someone dies, a politician exposes a danger from the old pits.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterdamp is the poisonous gas, chiefly carbon monoxide, left in a coal pit after an explosion.

clue.text: Picasso's intimate address

parts.note: an address sounds like a place where the painter lived, but it is the form of name his friends would call him by

explanation.walkthrough: 'address' sounds like a home, but means a form of name: friends would use the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Close friends used the Spanish painter's given name rather than his surname.

clue.text: Raised in group pedantry

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words group pedantry

explanation.surface: A fussy group is getting worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To up something is to increase it, so upped means increased.

clue.text: Small trendy gardens in America where British queens spent formative years

definitions.text: where British queens spent formative years

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
hip means fashionable
Americans call a garden a yard

explanation.surface: Fashionable American gardens are where the royal ladies grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: The queens are ocean liners such as the Queen Mary and Queen Elizabeth 2, built at British yards on the Clyde.
explanation.definitionFit: Liners named after queens were built and launched in dockyards, which is where they took shape.

clue.text: Once more finds out why rear lens is faulty

indicators.note: is faulty means is defective, so the letters of rear lens are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A photographer discovers again why the back lens of a camera is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn something again is to discover it a second time.

clue.text: Rapidly kidnaps famous London statue — heavens above!

indicators.note: kidnaps means seizes and holds, so the word for rapidly takes the statue inside it

parts.note: apace means quickly
Eros is the winged statue at Piccadilly Circus in London

explanation.surface: Someone swiftly makes off with a famous London landmark, to cries of astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavens above!' looks like an exclamation of surprise but defines the sky and space overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerospace is the earth's atmosphere and outer space together, the heavens overhead.

clue.text: Spring in wall heater

definitions.meaning: a hot natural fountain that erupts from the ground
a British gas appliance fixed to a wall that heats water

explanation.definitionFit: A natural hot spring that spouts, and a domestic gas water-heater in older British homes, share one name.

clue.text: Prepare a little butter for young student

parts.note: to school someone is to train or prepare them
a butter is an animal that butts, and a little one is a young goat

explanation.surface: Get ready a small pat of butter for the youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but something that butts; a young goat is a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at school, especially a young one, is a schoolchild.

clue.text: Miss west's classical sculptured form — not right, but majestic in play

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star; her name with the possessive gives these letters

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for right is removed from the statue form

parts.note: a torso is a classical sculpture of the trunk without head or limbs

explanation.surface: A film actress's classical statue loses something yet appears grand on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss west' is the actress Mae West. 'not' removes R (right) from TORSO to give TOSO. 'in play' means as a direction to performing musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is an Italian musical direction telling performers to play in a stately, majestic manner.

clue.text: They're set to return. Plunging in river?

indicators.note: plunging in means diving inside, so the river's letter goes into the reversed letters
return means go back, so the words set to are read in reverse

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Some creatures are due to come back, diving into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SET TO into OTTES; 'Plunging in' puts R (river) inside it. The whole clue also pictures these animals coming back to British rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to the creatures the rest of the clue describes, river mammals that swim and dive.

clue.text: Arab's weaving the best cloth

indicators.note: weaving means winding in and out, so the letters of Arab are woven into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
A means first-class, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: An Arab is weaving the finest fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab's' is 'Arab is', so the 's gives no letter; 'weaving' rearranges ARAB to BARA, then THE and A (best).
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric with a broken rib weave, used for uniforms.

clue.text: People in general sit up when praying

parts.note: man means humankind, people in general

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so the word sit runs backwards

explanation.surface: Everyone stands up straight when they say their prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal in a down clue. The definition leans on the insect's full name, the praying mantis, so 'when praying' points to it rather than defining it in strict dictionary terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect is named for holding its forelegs folded as if in prayer, hence the praying mantis.

clue.text: Serbs! You heartlessly turn on minions sapped of energy?

indicators.note: heartlessly means with the middle removed, so only the outside letters of you remain

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

indicators.note: sapped of means drained of, so the letter for energy is taken out of the word for minions

parts.note: slaves are minions, servile followers
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An outburst at the Serbs: you cruelly turn on exhausted underlings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves YU from YOU; 'sapped of' removes E (energy) from SLAVES to leave SLAVS.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbs were citizens of the former federation of South Slav nations that broke up in the 1990s.

clue.text: Dare say the Americans believe it

definitions.meaning: to dare say is to suppose or reckon
in American speech the phrase I reckon or I think is commonly put another way with this verb

explanation.definitionFit: To suppose or estimate something, and the American idiom for thinking so, share one verb.

clue.text: Psychological probe reveals Latin-American

indicators.note: a probe looking inside the word psychological reveals letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: A psychological examination exposes someone's origins.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholo is a term in the Americas for a person of mixed Indigenous and Spanish heritage.

clue.text: Space traveller seen to arrive on time

indicators.note: on in a down clue means placed above, so the word for arrive sits on top of the time letter

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: An astronaut is noticed turning up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen to' is padding linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is a body of ice and dust that journeys round the sun through space.

clue.text: Wrong name on drug, medicine to get you going

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the rearranged name follows the drug's letter

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so the letters of name are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A pharmacist puts the wrong name on a drug, a remedy to get you moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' is the anagram signal; E is crossword slang for ecstasy, and 'on' in an across clue sets the jumbled word after it. The definition jokes that the remedy gets the bowels moving.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema flushes the bowel, a treatment used to relieve constipation.

clue.text: Rifle returned to producer — skilled artisan

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for rifle is read backwards

parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or plunder, so loot
a maker is one who produces

explanation.surface: A gun goes back to its manufacturer, a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' looks like a gun but is a verb, to plunder, giving LOOT; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolmaker is a skilled worker who makes and repairs precision tools and dies.

clue.text: Sadie's not nice, wrecking festival

indicators.note: wrecking means smashing up, so the letters of Sadie's not nice are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Sadie is being unpleasant and spoiling the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascensiontide is the Christian season around Ascension Day, a church feast.
